#   SELECT cnpj_basico FROM workspace.default.hub_empresa
#   ORDER BY sha2(concat(cnpj_basico, '20260812'), 256) LIMIT 1024
# -- statement 01f1986b-c653-17e7-8c1d-807a684b8f45, from_cache: None.
#
# WHY IT IS PINNED RATHER THAN RE-QUERIED. opl.generator.cnpj_pool imports no pyspark and
# no databricks SDK, and running the query belongs to the caller; the caller here is a
# host-side seeder that must run with no Databricks credential at all, so that
# `docker compose up && pytest -m postgres` works on a clean checkout. The draw is already
# deterministic in (size=1024, seed=20260812), so this file is a CROSS-CHECK and not a
# weakening: a re-query that disagrees with it is a FINDING, not a reason to refresh it.
#
# SORTED, because opl.generator.cnpj_pool.validated_pool sorts and the generator picks
# counterparties BY INDEX -- pool order decides which company gets which payment.
#
# 142 of these 1,024 keys carry a LEADING ZERO (min 00057343). Any column, cast or parse
# that treats a CNPJ as a number destroys them silently. That is why the Postgres merchant
# table types `cnpj` as text.
#
# Lines beginning with # are stripped by the reader before validated_pool() sees them.
